title: Read regional wages with their period and source method
question: What do employed workers earn in the economic regions around these places?
dek: Job Bank low, median and high wages, grouped by comparable period and methodology.

findings.headline: Registered nurses: comparable regional medians range from $39.38 to $58.00 per hour
findings.detail: Among 30 economic regions using Labour Force Survey, reference period 2023-2024: Capitale-Nationale has $39.38/hour and Northwest Territories has $58.00/hour. These are regional wages of employed workers, not city pay or starting salaries.
findings.calc: Distinct economic regions; identical hourly unit, observation period and methodology; largest comparable cohort for this occupation.

findings.headline: Welders: comparable regional medians range from $25.00 to $39.90 per hour
findings.detail: Among 19 economic regions using Labour Force Survey, reference period 2023-2024: Prince Edward Island has $25.00/hour and Edmonton has $39.90/hour. These are regional wages of employed workers, not city pay or starting salaries.
findings.calc: Distinct economic regions; identical hourly unit, observation period and methodology; largest comparable cohort for this occupation.

findings.headline: Transport truck drivers: comparable regional medians range from $20.00 to $34.00 per hour
findings.detail: Among 28 economic regions using Labour Force Survey, reference period 2023-2024: Fredericton--Oromocto has $20.00/hour and Yukon Territory has $34.00/hour. These are regional wages of employed workers, not city pay or starting salaries.
findings.calc: Distinct economic regions; identical hourly unit, observation period and methodology; largest comparable cohort for this occupation.

interpretation: Economic-region wages provide context around a city; they are not city-level estimates or an offer a newcomer should expect.
Compare wages only when the occupation, hourly or annual basis, period and source method agree. Annual cells are kept in the data but excluded from these hourly charts.
methodology: The source edition is discovered through the official open.canada.ca catalog. Each wage cell retains Reference_Period and Data_Source_E from the CSV.
For each chart, keep the largest cohort of distinct economic regions with the same period and methodology. Regions are listed alphabetically; provincial and national fallbacks are not substituted.
limitations: Different methods or periods are not pooled into a single ranking. Published periods in this snapshot: 2021, 2023-2024, 2024
Wages are nominal earnings of employed workers; they are not adjusted for regional living costs and exclude benefits. Some occupations and regions have no published estimate.

title: Job markets differ by several points between Canadian cities, and the year-on-year moves are mostly small
question: Which cities have tighter labour markets, and how are conditions changing?
dek: Labour Force Survey rates for comparable whole-CMA areas, with other places shown on their published geography.

findings.headline: Unemployment ranges from 4.0% in Sherbrooke to 9.3% in Kelowna (three months to 2026-09)
findings.detail: Across 23 CMAs the seasonally adjusted three-month average unemployment rate runs from 4.0% (Sherbrooke) to 9.3% (Kelowna); the middle is about 6.4%. Employment rates (share of everyone 15+ who is working) range from 57.5% in London to 66.8% in Calgary, which also reflects age structure and who is in the labour force. Ottawa-Gatineau parts are shown separately from whole-CMA ranks. Differences of one point or less between nearby cities are often within sampling error.
findings.calc: Table 14-10-0459-01, seasonally adjusted, Estimate, REF_DATE 2026-09; unemployment rate and employment rate for whole-CMA places on the same geography; territories, Charlottetown (provincial) and Brandon (regional, unadjusted) excluded from the ranking.

findings.headline: Compared with a year earlier, unemployment fell in 14 of 23 places and rose in 9, but only 5 changes are clearly larger than sampling noise
findings.detail: Changes beyond 1.96 standard errors: Windsor -3.1 pp, Toronto -1.9 pp, Calgary -1.8 pp, Winnipeg -1.4 pp, London +2.1 pp. Every other change is small relative to the survey's sampling error and should not be read as a trend. Both values are three-month moving averages, so a one-month swing is dampened and consecutive months overlap.
findings.calc: change = rate(2026-09) - rate(2025-09) from 14-10-0459-01 (SA, 3-month moving average); significant if |change| > 1.96 x published standard error of year-over-year change; whole-CMA places.

interpretation: A lower unemployment rate and a higher employment rate usually mean employers compete harder for workers, but rates describe everyone in the labour force, not newcomers in your occupation. Check Job Bank wages and current postings for your field.
Treat gaps of a point or less as ties. Small metropolitan areas have larger sampling error, and the three-month moving average smooths month-to-month changes.

For Whitehorse, Yellowknife and Iqaluit the figures are territory-wide; Charlottetown shows Prince Edward Island; Brandon shows the Southwest economic region (unadjusted). They sit in the map and place profiles with that label rather than in the rankings.
methodology: Source: Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey, Table 14-10-0459-01 (CMA, three-month moving average, seasonally adjusted), latest period 2026-09; release date is shown in Sources. Territories: Table 14-10-0292-01 (seasonally adjusted series); Brandon: Table 14-10-0462-01 (economic region, unadjusted).

Each rate is the three-month moving average ending in the month shown. The one-year change subtracts the same measure twelve months earlier; significance uses Statistics Canada's standard error of the year-over-year change.
Ottawa and Gatineau use the LFS's Ontario and Quebec parts of the Ottawa-Gatineau CMA.
limitations: The LFS is a sample survey; estimates for small metros are volatile and Statistics Canada rounds to one decimal. Levels and changes are not forecasts.

Rates describe all residents 15+, including students, retirees and people outside the labour force, and say little about opportunities for a specific occupation or for people who are not yet in Canada.

For Nunavut the published seasonally adjusted values equal the unadjusted values in every month since 2019 (and in about a third of months for the Northwest Territories), so the SA label is largely nominal there.
